claims.sentence: Hepatitis C is an infection with a virus that causes inflammation of the liver, which can damage the liver over time.
Hepatitis C is a virus that causes inflammation of the liver, and over time the inflamed liver can become damaged.
Most people with hepatitis C have no symptoms, so many people do not know they have it.
It is spread through contact with infected blood.
It is diagnosed with a blood test, and treatment is a short course of antiviral tablets.
Without treatment it can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer.
Hepatitis C is caused by a virus that is spread through contact with infected blood.
Casual contact does not spread the virus, and it is not passed on through breast milk, food or water, according to WHO.
Sharing drug-injecting equipment.
Having medical care abroad, in a part of the world where hepatitis C is more common.

claims.sentence: Hepatitis C is diagnosed using two blood tests, an antibody test and a PCR test.

claims.sentence: Most people with hepatitis C have no symptoms.
Because of this, many people do not know they have the virus.
When symptoms do appear, they can take weeks, months or even years to start.
Early symptoms can include a high temperature, tiredness, tummy pain, loss of appetite, feeling or being sick, and yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes, which is called jaundice.
Among people who get early symptoms, around 1 in 5 have jaundice.

notes: BLT page was returned only once by a BLT-restricted query, and only as a summary; its 8 to 12 weeks and 8 in 10 acute-no-symptoms points were taken from that summary. Treatment cure rates differ between NHS pages (9 in 10 vs more than 95%); both attributed. Removed 1 in 4 clearance (sources said 15-20%) and the NHS England 2030 target (not confirmed; 2030 is the WHO global goal). Transfusion dates differ between sources (1991 BLT, 1996 NHS) so none given. Some ledger URLs were not re-retrieved (NHS main page sentences are supported via search summaries that blended pages); the NHS England 2023 home-test reference was dropped because no search returned it; the NHS England 2021 children page was returned. Reviewer may wish to verify the 'seekCare' GP sentence on the live NHS page (classed textbook route-to-care). The related link to cirrhosis is kept (complication per MedlinePlus).
